resources.string: Your own face for the Boox sleep screen, typeset for the panel and kept up to date while you use the tablet.
A full-screen face. Boox shows it as its screensaver picture and reads it fresh at every sleep.
A paper plate laid over what was on screen, through the Boox Transparent style and its sticker. Kept current through Shizuku, or with your permission to write the sticker.
The weekday, a big day number, the month with today marked, and what is coming up.
A Braun tuning scale for the battery, with the date and ruled readings below.
The weekday set as large as the panel allows, over the quote of the day or your own.
Leaves the top of the screen to the live Boox clock, which Boox refreshes every 5 minutes while asleep. Set Clock style to Digital in Boox for this face.
Your picture, filled or fitted, with an optional caption band along the bottom.
Your note, set as large as it fits.
Who to return the tablet to if it is found. Best on a tablet that leaves the house.
Only the date and the lamp.
Plates are drawn on a transparent sheet with a soft paper edge, so they stay legible over any page underneath.
When the tablet was last in use. It is rounded down to the refresh step, and exact with Sleep now.
From your calendars, the coming seven days.
Calendar access is off, so events stay hidden until you allow it.
A short public-domain line, a new one each day.
Leave room for the Boox clock
Keeps the top of the screen free, for a live time from Boox\'s own clock.
That picture could not be read.
Boox dithers every picture itself. Pre-dithering spreads the photo over 16 levels per colour first, which can look finer on Kaleido; the text stays undithered either way.
Faces use real weights of the chosen typeface, including every instance of a variable font. Fonts you keep in Fonts appear here.
The accent fills the lamp, today\'s date and the needle. Kaleido shows solid colour areas best, so text always stays black or white.
While the tablet is awake, redraw every

Boox reads the picture when the tablet goes to sleep and never again until it wakes, so on its own nothing on it changes while asleep; the live updates below change that. The face is also redrawn when the battery, the date, the calendar, the rotation or your settings change, and not at all when nothing on it would change.
A Braun-style wall clock that keeps time while the tablet sleeps, with the date, the battery and how long it has slept. Without updates while asleep, the hands show when it was put down.
The time set as large as the panel allows, the date under it, and the battery, time asleep and the next event along the foot. Without updates while asleep, it shows when the tablet was put down.
A readout of the sleep itself: how long, the battery on a tuning scale with what it has used and the rate, the next event counted down and the next alarm. It needs updates while asleep to move.
How long the tablet has slept, and the battery it has used. Shown with updates while asleep.
Drawn by the same renderer as the sleep screen, shown as it reads 1 h 25 min into a sleep with updates while asleep on. Tap it to see it at full size.
This face is made for updates while asleep. Turn them on below to keep it moving.

Live updates redraw the face while the tablet sleeps, so the date, battery and agenda stay true, and Boox’s charging bar is covered (so is Boox’s own clock, if you show one). The time you put the tablet down stays as it was. Each update wakes the panel for about a second and a half — measured on this tablet at about 1.6 mAh an hour at the one-minute step, a fifth of that at five — which is why one minute is kept for charging.
One minute is used while charging. On battery the shortest step is %1$d minutes, which is what keeps the panel from waking sixty times an hour.
No wake-ups on battery at all
Android hides app windows behind the lock screen, except accessibility overlays. The service only holds the picture: it can’t read the screen or your typing and does nothing while the screen is on.
Boox deletes the wake-up alarms of apps it restricts. Allow background usage on Android’s battery page; if updates still don’t arrive, switch it off and on once.
So updates land on the minute
The service is allowed but Android hasn’t started it yet. Leaving this page and coming back usually does it.
Live updates redraw the full-screen picture; the Transparent sticker can’t be updated this way.
Apply a face first; live updates redraw the face you applied.
No sleep with live updates yet.

resources.string: Last sleep: no updates were due.

The last sleep got no updates: Boox’s power manager most likely cleared the alarm. Switch Allow background usage off and on again on the battery page, or use Register with Boox, then try another sleep.
Keeps the sleep screen current while the tablet sleeps

Lets BooxUltimatum redraw its sleep screen every few minutes while the tablet is locked. Android hides ordinary app windows behind the lock screen; an accessibility overlay is the only window it doesn’t hide, so this service exists only to hold that picture. It can’t read what’s on screen, doesn’t see your typing and performs no actions. It shows nothing while the screen is on.
This face is now the sleep screen.

The plate is written to Boox\'s own sticker. BooxUltimatum can\'t read which screensaver style Boox is set to, so if Transparent isn\'t chosen there (with the sticker on), you\'ll still see whatever picture Boox was showing before.
Back to the Boox default picture. Choose your former style in Boox\'s screensaver settings.
Sleep now needs Shizuku. Over Transparent can also work through the sticker permission below.
Mode changed. Tap Apply to hand the new mode to Boox; until then the last picture stays and is no longer redrawn.
Checked %1$s · nothing on the face changed, so the file was left as it is
Drawn by the same renderer as the published picture. Dashes mark where Boox draws its clock when you leave room for it. Tap it to see it at full size.

For a clean face, open Boox screensaver settings, set Clock style and Text display to None, and turn Bottom status bar off (it adds the battery and “Press power button to wake up”; Boox still shows it while the tablet is charging, whatever the setting). To keep a live time instead, leave Clock style on Digital and turn on Leave room for the Boox clock, or use Under the clock.
Boox needs you to choose the sticker once. After that BooxUltimatum keeps it up to date.

BooxUltimatum can\'t see which style Boox is on. Until Boox itself is set to Transparent with the sticker on, Boox keeps showing the last sleep picture it was given — so after a switch from Sleep image, that older picture is what a sleep will show.

If an older BooxUltimatum picture is still in Pictures, the app can\'t remove it: Android won\'t let an app change a picture it no longer owns, so the newest copy is written beside it and the old one is yours to delete in Files.
Tap Put in Sticker album below. The current plate appears in the gallery\'s Sticker album.
Open Boox screensaver settings, choose Transparent, turn on Show lockscreen sticker, then Select sticker, the + tile, the Sticker album and the BooxUltimatum picture, and confirm the crop with OK.
Come back here and tap Apply. BooxUltimatum finds the sticker Boox saved and redraws it for you.
The plate is in the Sticker album.

The Boox clock, the motto and the bottom status bar are drawn by Boox over any style; each can be turned off in Boox screensaver settings. Restore can\'t read back the style you had before, so it sets the Boox default picture; pick your former style in Boox afterwards.
With a PIN, a tablet put to sleep from the lock screen shows a black privacy screen instead. That is Boox\'s choice and outside this app.
Shizuku is running, so the plate is written through it. Nothing else is needed.
BooxUltimatum finds the sticker Boox saved by looking in the Sticker album. Allow it to read pictures for that: nothing else is looked at.
Android will ask once whether BooxUltimatum may change Boox\'s sticker picture. Saying yes keeps the plate current without Shizuku.
BooxUltimatum may write the sticker itself, so no Shizuku is needed for the plate.
No sticker is visible in Boox\'s album. If Android was told to share only some pictures, allow all of them; otherwise do the four steps above first.
Android did not allow changing the sticker picture, so the plate can\'t be kept current on its own. Start Shizuku from Access instead.

Boox draws the sticker over the whole panel, keeping the middle. Plates stay inside that band, so one file is right in both orientations. In Boox\'s screensaver settings the scale choice can also be set to fit, which shows the whole sheet.
Write a note in BooxUltimatum › Sleep to show it here.
Choose a picture in BooxUltimatum › Sleep.
This needs Shizuku. Start it from Access, then try again.
No Boox sticker yet. Follow the steps under Boox settings to choose the BooxUltimatum sticker once.
Could not stage the plate in the app\'s own files.
BooxUltimatum may not write Boox\'s sticker yet. Let it write the sticker under Boox settings, or start Shizuku from Access, then apply again.
Could not read the sticker Boox made, so it was left untouched.
The sticker was not written. Check that Boox\'s sticker is still where it was, then apply again.
Could not put Boox\'s own sticker back: %1$s. Boox\'s screensaver settings can choose another picture.
Sleep screen set to the %1$s face, as the Boox sleep picture
Sleep screen set to the %1$s plate, over the Boox Transparent style
Sleep screen handed back to the Boox default picture
Power-off screen set to the %1$s face
Power-off screen handed back to the Boox default
The Boox power-off screen is back

What the tablet shows when it’s switched off. Boox keeps a copy of the picture, so it stays as it was when you set it: the battery and put-down time are left out, and after changing the face, update it again.

A cube clock drawn in true perspective: the time on the side facing you, the date on the side in shade, an accent button on top and a shadow in stipple or hatching. Without updates while asleep, it shows when the tablet was put down.
Hours and minutes on split-flap cards, the upper flap leaning back on its hinge, with the date on small flaps below. Without updates while asleep, it shows when the tablet was put down.

A grid of tiles you choose below: the time, the date and week, the battery and what it has used, time asleep, the alarm, what’s next, how far through the day and the year, the moon, and the home screen’s weather with the time it was read.
The time in words, lit in a grid of letters, in steps of five minutes; accent dots count the minutes in between. The letters are in English.
The whole day on one 24-hour ring: today’s events as arcs, the sleep so far in the accent, now as a hand, and the night shaded once the home screen has a weather city.
Today along a line: events as blocks, the sleep so far in the accent and a marker for now, with the time and readings above.
A Braun-style LCD clock with drawn seven-segment figures, small fields for the date, time asleep, battery and alarm, and a row of keys with one in the accent.

Today’s sun and tonight’s moon. The sun’s path, sunrise and sunset are worked out on the tablet for the home screen’s weather city, the only place the app knows; without one, the sun follows the clock and the face says so. The moon’s phase needs no place.

A newspaper front page: the next event as the headline (or the quote), the weather and battery in the masthead’s ears, and columns for the sleep, what’s ahead and the almanac. The issue number is the day of the year.
The year at a glance, every day a dot: the past filled, today in the accent, and how far through the year you are.
The 24-hour dial turns its hour hand once a day, with midnight at the top.
The time and date always show. Weather appears when the home screen has read it in the last three days, and next events need calendar access.
Words go in steps of five minutes and the dots add the minutes in between. Updates while asleep land on a round five, so there the dots stay dark.
Sunrise and sunset need a weather city on the home screen; it’s the only place the app knows.
Without calendar access or an event this week, the quote of the day takes the headline.
The sun stays up all day
The sun stays down all day
